items.excerpt: HarperCollins CEO Brian Murray called for industrywide best practices on AI-assisted authorship, warning that an AI-assisted book 'could very well be treated as a book in the public domain.' He argued publishers, agents and authors must agree on standards rather than wait for a technical detection fix.

A debut author's $2M+ two-book deal was canceled after agents concluded the manuscript was substantially AI-assisted. Industry insiders now estimate roughly half of submissions are heavily AI-assisted, with no standard way to verify human authorship.

OpenAI has begun blocking ChatGPT requests to write 'in the style of' named living authors. Style isn't explicitly protected by copyright, but the move reads as a defensive step amid ongoing author litigation.

Anthropic will add embedded watermarks and digitally signed provenance metadata to Claude output to satisfy EU AI transparency rules. For authors drafting with Claude, that means AI provenance may travel with the text itself.

Dan Holloway unpacks Tuhin Chakrabarty's viral study of 14,419 self-published Amazon titles, which found AI-generated books are commercially viable but consistently outsold by human-written ones. The paper's real target is how AI volume dilutes indie authors' discoverability.

Roohi Ghosh asks what 'author voice' still means once AI writing assistance sits alongside heavy editing and peer revision in the publishing pipeline. The piece argues publishers need a working definition of authorial voice before they can police it.

Generative AI is driving a 'synthetic consensus' in which flawed claims gain credibility through cheap repetition faster than the literature can correct itself. The author flags model collapse as publishing's compounding-error risk.

Online AI-authorship suspicion has fallen disproportionately on writers from underrepresented backgrounds, sparking a trade-wide debate. Agents and authors say unreliable AI detection is turning into a reputational hazard.

STM chief executive Caroline Sutton warned academic publishers against an escalating 'war of AI against AI' in research integrity screening. She urged blending automated detection with human review of suspect submissions.

A roundup of the week's AI-in-publishing moves: Anthropic's Claude watermarking plan, Substack's Pangram AI-detection rollout, and the EU push for machine-readable AI markers. Together they sketch a provenance layer arriving across writing platforms.

Library-world news roundup led by a study in which readers gave higher ratings to AI-generated stories they believed were human-written. The finding complicates the assumption that readers can protect the market by taste alone.
A 404 Media investigation found Amazon buying books in bulk and destructively scanning them — cutting off spines — to build AI training corpora. Rare and out-of-print titles are among the casualties.

Dale L. Roberts walks indie authors through how new European AI transparency regulations are reaching Claude users worldwide. The episode also covers a study challenging assumptions about AI-generated writing and a record number of Pulitzer winners disclosing AI use.

Episode 50 of The Automated Author digs into Claude's AI text watermarking and how Anthropic's approach may nudge word choice itself. Elizabeth Ann West and Stacey Anderson argue those 'low-stakes' vocabulary decisions are anything but low-stakes in fiction.
